record.title: DeltaSelect paper reports a budgeted task subset for repeat coding-agent A/B tests
record.summary: A paper introduces DeltaSelect, which ranks tasks using resampled one-run correlations with full-benchmark scores, calibrates fractional verifier results, then selects tasks under a cost budget for repeated baseline-versus-candidate comparisons. In one author-reported Agent Layer case study, 13 eight-task evaluations led to a configuration with a 58.1% lower recorded cost and a higher calibrated score than the initial custom skills/instructions. The paper also finds substantial mismatch between published DeepSWE estimates and a Codex target harness. These are bounded paper-reported results; the implementation was not run in this review.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: DeltaSelect ranks tasks by the fifth-percentile Pearson correlation across 10,000 deterministic resamples, calibrates fractional verifier results to a common full-score scale, and greedily selects tasks within a configured budget. On the DeepSWE snapshot the authors report that 22 of 113 tasks reached a fifth-percentile correlation of at least 0.50.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: In 13 eight-task evaluations of one gpt-5.6-luna low-reasoning Agent Layer skills/instructions case study, the authors report a final configuration with a 42.36% calibrated score at $1.75, compared with the initial custom bundle at 36.46% and $4.18. The analysis uses one endpoint run per task and transfers variance estimates from published mini-swe-agent runs.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: For the same eight tasks and gpt-5.6-luna settings, paper-reported Codex-harness costs were 1.5 to 3.5 times the corresponding DeepSWE estimates; scores also differed. The paper cautions these comparisons establish a planning mismatch, not a causal estimate of the harness effect.

claims.label: DEMONSTRATED
claims.text: The arXiv paper links a public Agent Layer repository and DeltaSelect implementation page. The repository README identifies itself as an open-source coding-agent orchestration project; this review did not run its code.

evidence_gaps.description: No independent team reproduced the selector, case-study endpoints or reported costs in this review.
The selector was not compared with random, cheapest-first or median-correlation selection at equal cost; ranking and published-data example use the same DeepSWE snapshot.

The case study covers one model family, one custom harness and one skill/instruction bundle; endpoint uncertainty uses transferred published variance and some iterations changed multiple instructions.
The paper links public code, but no repository code or study artifacts were run or independently audited in this review.

brief.importance_rationale: If validated across benchmarks and harnesses, an affordable fixed task set could make coding-agent workflow changes easier to compare repeatedly; this is one author-reported method and case study with untested selector alternatives and limited transfer evidence.
limitations: The task selector and calibration choices are not shown to outperform alternative selectors at matched cost; the paper names those comparisons as future work.
The published-data projection uses the same DeepSWE snapshot to construct and assess selection, so the evidence is in-sample.

The Agent Layer case study has one run per endpoint task, transfers variance from mini-swe-agent, and changes more than one instruction in several evaluations; it does not establish a causal effect of a single edit.
A small fixed task set may omit capabilities, magnify task-quality problems and induce specialization; it is not a broad benchmark or safety evaluation.
The repository was inspected at README level only; no code, data, or evaluation was executed in this review.
brief.summary: A paper introduces DeltaSelect, which ranks tasks using resampled one-run correlations with full-benchmark scores, calibrates fractional verifier results, then selects tasks under a cost budget for repeated baseline-versus-candidate comparisons. In one author-reported Agent Layer case study, 13 eight-task evaluations led to a configuration with a 58.1% lower recorded cost and a higher calibrated score than the initial custom skills/instructions. The paper also finds substantial mismatch between published DeepSWE estimates and a Codex target harness. These are bounded paper-reported results; the implementation was not run in this review.

technical.claimed_result: Authors report 22 of 113 DeepSWE tasks with fifth-percentile correlation >=0.50. In a 13-evaluation, eight-task Agent Layer case study, reported recorded cost declined 58.1% ($4.18 to $1.75) while calibrated score rose from 36.46% to 42.36%. The study uses single-run endpoints and transferred variance estimates.
technical.compute_or_cost: Paper reports $27.86 total model cost across 13 case-study evaluations at the stated August 16, 2026 rates. Initial and adopted eight-task endpoints are $4.18 and $1.75 respectively. Costs from published mini-swe-agent estimates did not transfer directly: paper reports Codex costs 1.5–3.5 times higher for the same eight tasks and settings.
technical.demonstrated_result: The accessible arXiv paper and linked public repository README establish that the paper and a code repository are published. Reported benchmark and case-study values are author claims; this review did not execute or reproduce the implementation.
technical.mechanism: DeltaSelect resamples one trial per task and configuration to estimate each task's conservative correlation with full benchmark scores, maps task-level fractional verifier results to a common score using linear calibration, weights by calibration residuals, and scans a fixed reliability ranking under a dollar budget. The task set and scoring specification are then frozen for baseline-versus-candidate comparisons.
technical.novelty: The paper combines conservative task ranking from repeated trial resampling, per-task fractional-score calibration, cost-constrained allocation, and target-harness baseline validation for frequent within-system coding-agent comparisons. The paper cites prior benchmark reduction and active-testing methods and frames its contribution as their combination for this use case rather than a universal evaluator.
technical.regime: DeepSWE v1.1 snapshot: 22,586 source trials, 22,417 usable trials, 18 models, 50 model-effort configurations and 113 tasks. Method resamples one of four trials per complete task-configuration cell 10,000 times. Target-harness study uses eight selected tasks; Agent Layer case study uses 13 evaluations at gpt-5.6-luna low reasoning. No independent replication reviewed.
technical.reproducibility: The paper links a public Agent Layer repository and interactive DeltaSelect page, describes the DeepSWE data snapshot, method and study provenance, but the code and data were not run or audited here. Cheapest next action is a pinned reproduction and equal-cost selector comparison on a held-out benchmark.
technical.strongest_baseline: For the eight-task case study the paper compares initial and adopted Agent Layer skill/instruction configurations under the same stated model, reasoning level, tasks, calibration and weights. The adopted endpoint is $1.75 and 42.36% calibrated score versus $4.18 and 36.46% initially. Each endpoint has one run per task, and uncertainty is transferred from repeated mini-swe-agent data.

brief.title: DeltaSelect paper reports a budgeted task subset for repeat coding-agent A/B tests
brief.why_it_matters: If independently validated, fixed low-cost task subsets could support more frequent coding-agent workflow comparisons. The paper's own data show that task reliability varies and that scores and prices from one harness did not transfer to another. The selector's advantage over alternatives and its usefulness beyond one benchmark, model family and custom harness remain unknown.
